label: early copy step echoing o/p/j/t while outputting n/u/o/g (short seqs)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.001% of steps), firing only in the copy phase and only early in it (recall_idx 1-3, mostly 1, i.e. the step right after the first token is echoed back). The input is nearly always o, p, j or t, and the token being output and the next one are usually from n, u, o, g, v. It is strongest on short sequences (L=3-4) whose first token is o or p followed by n/u/g, e.g. o n u <DEL> [o]. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and never on first occurrences of the input token. The context description (copy, recall_idx<=3, input in {o,p,j,t}, output in {n,u,o,g,v}) covers about 89% of activation mass but has precision 0.2%. The narrow recorded predicate reaches about 20% precision and 27% recall, so whatever selects the few firing cases among these contexts is not captured.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: o, p, j, t, r, -; least: y, i, n, <DEL>) and the second original token (most: n, o, y, v, u, i; least: r, z, 3, p); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=1, L=4 & t=5.
